beats.say: Out of every hundred dollars TSMC sells, how much does it keep? Not ten. Not twenty five. Fifty one dollars, after paying for its factories, its engineers and its taxes. A year ago, it kept about forty six. So how does a company that runs factories keep half of everything it sells?

beats.say: In three months, TSMC billed forty six point seven billion dollars. Of every hundred, about sixty eight came from chips for A I and data centres, which TSMC calls high performance computing. About twenty one came from smartphones. Cars, devices and the rest: about eleven.
beats.cap: In three months, TSMC billed $46.7 billion. Of every $100, about $68 came from chips for AI and data centres, which TSMC calls high-performance computing. About $21 came from smartphones. Cars, devices and the rest: about $11.

beats.say: Chips are made on processes named in nanometres. Smaller is newer, and harder to make. Of every hundred dollars of wafers TSMC sold, thirty three were three nanometre chips. Twenty eight were five nanometre. Ten were seven. The newest, two nanometres, is already eight. Older processes: twenty one.

beats.say: Take one hundred dollars of TSMC's sales. Making the chips, the materials, the power, and the machines wearing out, took about thirty three dollars sixty. Running the company, research, sales and offices, took seven eighty. Tax, after a little interest income, took seven sixty. Kept as profit: fifty one dollars.
